candidates.detail: SettledDrape derives Deserialize over packed arrays; the packed decoder checks base64 and whole-record byte lengths but does not call SettledDrape::validate. That validator would reject a binding triangle ordinal outside the saved body triangle count. Public SettledDrape::wear instead calls fit directly, and fit checks only that the input body vertex and triangle counts equal the saved counts before placing each binding. Wearer::frame passes the binding ordinal to TriangleBvh::triangle, which directly indexes the triangle vector. A decoded binding ordinal 1 with saved and input body counts of three vertices and one triangle therefore indexes the one-element triangle list out of range if a caller omits validate and reaches placement. No product decode, wear, BVH operation or panic was executed.
candidates.witness_and_path: The preserved reconstructed JSON has three finite cloth positions, three UV rows, one valid cloth face, three whole six-word binding records and body counts {vertices: 3, triangles: 1}; its first binding names triangle 1. The hypothetical input body is the finite triangle [0,1,2] on three positions, so count equality passes and normal/BVH construction sees valid body indices. Calling public wear on the directly decoded value without validate reaches binding 1; public drape_outfit also forwards an input.settled value to wear. The file is a newly constructed evidence illustration, not a recovered checkpoint record or a product test.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: SettledDrape::capture validates before returning. Wardrobe::load and insert call SettledGarment::validate; inspected CLI and studio recipe loaders call CharacterRecipe::validate, which traverses inventory article validation to the same saved-drape validator. These paths reject this malformed binding before ordinary loading completes. Other public decoding and wear callers, mutable body topology and actual malformed input reachability remain open.
